gaps.sentence: The box was empty — there was ___ inside.
gaps.explanation: 'Empty' explains 'there was nothing inside'; the other options contradict emptiness.

gaps.sentence: One of my shoes is tighter than ___.
gaps.hint: shoes come in pairs of two
gaps.explanation: 'One ... than the other' is the pattern for two items; 'another' would suggest more than two.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ at the door — go and see who it is.
gaps.explanation: 'Somebody' is used in affirmative sentences for an unknown person; 'anybody' belongs to questions and negatives.

gaps.sentence: The ___ of teenagers own a smartphone these days.
gaps.explanation: 'The majority of + plural noun' means most of them; 'the number of teenagers own' would be ungrammatical.

gaps.sentence: We had very ___ rain this spring, so the garden suffered.
gaps.explanation: 'Little' means not much and is used with uncountables; the garden suffering shows an insufficient amount.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ point asking him again — he never replies.
gaps.explanation: 'There's no point' — 'point' needs the adjective 'no', not the pronoun 'none'.

gaps.sentence: There are two cafes here, but ___ of them is open on Mondays.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of them is open' is correct for two items with a singular verb; 'both' and 'all' would need 'are'.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.
